CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SUBHASH CHAND -------
For the Petitioner : Mr. Indrajit Sinha, Advocate For the U.O.I. : Ms. Chandana Kumari, AC to ASGI --------
th Order No.09 /Dated: 14 June, 2024 1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned counsel for the C.B.I.
2.

This second bail application has been filed on behalf of the abovenamed applicant with prayer to release on bail in connection with R.C. Case No.05(S)/2022-R registered under Sections 120B read with 409, 420, 467, 468, 469 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code pending in the court of learned Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate-cum-Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ranchi.

entities.text: Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate-cum-Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ranchi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 11.04.2022 in B.A. No. 15078 of 2021.

By way of present bail application, the applicant has renewed his prayer for bail on the ground that after rejection of the first bail application, the investigation of the case was taken over by the C.B.I., charge-sheet has been filed and no one witness has been examined till date.
The applicant has been languishing in jail since 24.08.2021.
In view of the above, contended to enlarge the applicant on bail.

4. Learned counsel for the C.B.I. opposed the contentions made by the learned counsel for the applicant and contended that the charge-sheet was filed on 31.12.2023 and the period of incarceration cannot be taken into consideration.
5. The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 11.04.2022 in B.A. No. 15078 of 2021 on merit.
Admittedly, the charge-sheet has been filed in this case on Kameshwar Ram vs Union Of India Through C.B.I. .... .... ... on 14 June, 2024

entities.text: Kameshwar Ram vs Union Of India Through C.B.I.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the period of incarceration is concerned, the same cannot be accepted as a new ground taking into consideration the gravity of offence, in which, defalcation of Rs.2,10,41,382/- has been made.
6. In view of the submissions and materials available on record, no new ground is found in second bail application.
Accordingly, the same is hereby rejected.
7. As prayed by the learned counsel for the applicant, learned trial Court is directed to expedite the trial.

(Subhash Chand, J.) Madhav/-
